extracted.intended_audience: radio newscast producers, editors, and newsroom staff (NPR/newscast teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for choosing and producing stories for NPR's hourly newscasts, emphasizing what makes items newsworthy for listeners and how teams organize shifts and editorial decisions. Covers selection factors, stylistic standards for short-form audio, production workflow, and how personalization interacts with editorial curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevancy to the lives of listeners
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevancy to the lives of listeners
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary selection factor: stories should matter to listeners' everyday lives — practical impact and usefulness to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediacy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary selection factor: preference for events or developments that are current and timely; breaking news can override other considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: National appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: National appeal — must matter beyond a single locale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional filter: stories should have significance to a national audience rather than only local interest; local stories need extra attributes to break through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectacular or unique local story threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectacular or unique required for local stories to break through
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local items must be unusual, visually/sensorily striking, or otherwise exceptional to be included in a national newscast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interest / team engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Interesting / fun — engaging enough for the team
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional filter: producers/editors look for stories that engage the newsroom; 'interesting' or 'fun' pieces are more likely to be selected when they energize the team.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience curiosity — what would NPR audience want
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional filter: consider what the NPR audience specifically wants to hear; editorial judgment about audience tastes and curiosity guides selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newscast production cycle and editorial roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Newscast Production Cycle — A.M., Midday, P.M. teams; editorial meeting at start of each shift; producer leads and decides story lineup; override for breaking news; stories swapped throughout shift
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural guideline: each shift begins with an editorial meeting to set the lineup; the producer has final say over the lineup; breaking news can override planned stories; story priorities may change and be swapped during the shift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity (short sentences)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style standard: write for short-form audio — use concise sentences suitable for quick listening and tight time slots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity (no jargon)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style standard: avoid jargon and complex phrasing so listeners can immediately understand the story without needing background knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable listener empowerment
rubrics_metrics.description: Listener empowered 'to make a decision or take an action'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style standard: stories should aim to give listeners information that enables decisions or actions, increasing practical relevance and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio quality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style standard: strong technical and editorial audio standards — clear, well-recorded sound is required for broadcast; poor audio can disqualify a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice variety
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style standard: include varied voices (reporters, interviewees, distinct speakers) to maintain listener interest and convey perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sound elements where possible
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style standard: prefer stories that include compelling ambient sound, natural audio, or interview clips that add aural interest and drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice / sound potential
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit radio-specific newsworthiness: assess whether a story yields usable audio — does it produce interview clips or sounds that work on radio?

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity-amenable storytelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: prefer stories that can be effectively told in tight time windows (about 30–60 seconds) without losing clarity or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aural drama
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: stories with natural aural drama — distinctive sounds or sonic moments — help capture listener attention in short-form audio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear narrative arc for short form
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear narrative arc for short form
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: even very short pieces should have a recognizable beginning, middle and end so listeners grasp the story quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronounceable names
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit editorial practicality: choose stories where names and terms are easily pronounceable on air to avoid on-air errors and awkwardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listener identification (commute audience)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion: consider whether listeners (e.g., commuters) can identify with or relate to the story; relevance to typical listening contexts like commuting increases suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: National significance / significance beyond locale
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness: reinforce national appeal — the story should mean something to listeners across regions, not just locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freshness for breaking coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit temporal standard: breaking stories should be very recent (within the hour) to merit immediate inclusion and possible override of scheduled items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertaining for kicker stories
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit editorial taste: lighter or entertaining items are appropriate as 'kickers' at the end of a newscast to leave listeners with an engaging closing note.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPR One personalization + editorial curation
rubrics_metrics.description: NPR One combines editorial curation with user listening behavior, topic preferences, skip patterns, and time-of-day patterns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic guideline: story selection for personalized streams blends human editorial judgments with algorithmic signals (listening behavior, skips, time of day, topic preferences); editorial responsibility remains central despite personalization.
